national.canonicalTopic: Removal of Konda Surekha from Telangana Cabinet
national.headline: Konda Surekha is removed from the Telangana Cabinet
facts: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy removed Environment, Forests and Endowments Minister Konda Surekha from the Cabinet with immediate effect.
On the same date, the State Government withdrew G. Chinna Reddy’s appointment as Vice-Chairman of the Telangana State Planning Board.

Under Article 164, State Ministers are appointed by the Governor on the Chief Minister’s advice and hold office during the Governor’s pleasure; the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
national.summary: The Telangana Government made changes to the State Cabinet and the State Planning Board appointment.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Article 164(2) provides for collective responsibility of a State Council of Ministers to the Legislative Assembly.
national.mainsAngle: Relate the appointment and removal of State Ministers to constitutional conventions and responsible government.

sources.title: Konda Surekha Removed from Telangana Cabinet

national.notes:
# 1. Cabinet change
- **Who:** Telangana Chief Minister **A. Revanth Reddy** removed **Konda Surekha** from the Cabinet with immediate effect on **3 September 2026**.
- **Post:** **Environment, Forests and Endowments Minister**
- **Status:** **Completed**

# 2. Constitutional position
- **Constitutional basis:** Under **Article 164**, State Ministers are appointed by the **Governor** on the **Chief Minister’s advice** and hold office during the **Governor’s pleasure**.
- **Collective responsibility:** **Article 164(2)**; the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the **Legislative Assembly**.
- **Trap:** The Chief Minister advised the removal; under **Article 164**, the **Governor** is the formal appointing authority for State Ministers.

# 3. Related appointment and background
| **Action** | **Person / body** | **Details** |
|---|---|---|
| **Appointment withdrawn** | **G. Chinna Reddy** | **Vice-Chairman, Telangana State Planning Board**; appointment withdrawn by the **State Government** on **3 September 2026** |
| **Static constitutional links** | **Articles 163, 164 and 167** | **91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003** [GK] |

> Exam angle: Test the **Article 164** rules on appointment and collective responsibility alongside the Telangana Cabinet change.

national.canonicalTopic: Smriti Mandhana sets women’s international cricket run and century records
national.headline: Smriti Mandhana surpasses records for women’s international runs and centuries
facts: Smriti Mandhana scored 124 off 64 balls against Hong Kong in the Women’s T20 Asia Cup in Dubai on 2026-09-03.
Her international tally reached 10,880 runs, surpassing Mithali Raj’s 10,868.
Her 18th international century surpassed the 17 centuries recorded by Meg Lanning and Laura Wolvaardt.
The notes state that Mandhana became the first Indian woman cricketer to score international centuries in Tests, ODIs and T20Is.
national.summary: Mandhana’s innings against Hong Kong took her past Mithali Raj’s aggregate and gave her the highest international-century tally described in the notes.
national.staticLink: Mithali Raj made her international debut in 1999 and retired in 2022; the Women’s Asia Cup was first held in 2004.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The notes report Mandhana’s tally as 10,880 runs and 18 international centuries after the match.
national.mainsAngle: Women’s participation in elite sport and the growing visibility of women’s cricket records.

sources.title: Smriti Mandhana Sets Records for Most Runs and Centuries in Women’s International Cricket

national.notes:
# 1. Match and performance
- **Event:** **Women’s T20 Asia Cup**; **Smriti Mandhana** scored **124 off 64 balls** against **Hong Kong** in **Dubai** on **3 September 2026**.
- **Status:** **Final result**

# 2. International records
| **Record** | **Smriti Mandhana** | **Previous record / holder** |
|---|---|---|
| **International runs** | **10,880** | **Mithali Raj: 10,868** |
| **International centuries** | **18** | **Meg Lanning: 17; Laura Wolvaardt: 17** |
- **Milestone:** First **Indian woman cricketer** to score international centuries in **Tests, ODIs and T20Is**.
- **Trap:** The runs record and the centuries record are separate milestones; the previous holders differ.

# 3. Background
- **Mithali Raj:** International debut in **1999**; retired in **2022** [GK].
- **Women’s Asia Cup:** First held in **2004** [GK].
# 4. Also note
- Smriti Mandhana scored 124 off 64 balls against Hong Kong in the Women’s T20 Asia Cup in Dubai on 2026-09-03.
> Exam angle: Recall Mandhana’s **10,880-run** aggregate, **18 international centuries** and all-format century milestone.

national.headline: Defence Ministry releases ten-year RAKSHA diplomacy roadmap
facts: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh released the RAKSHA Defence Diplomacy Action Document in New Delhi on 3 September 2026.
The Ministry of Defence document sets out a ten-year roadmap for defence partnerships, security cooperation and defence manufacturing.
Its four pillars are Strategic Partnerships, Capacity Building, Indigenous Defence Exports and Maritime Security.
The maritime pillar includes Indian Ocean cooperation, disaster assistance, anti-piracy efforts and Maritime Domain Awareness.
national.summary: RAKSHA sets out a decade-long framework for linking India’s defence diplomacy with security partnerships, capacity building, exports and maritime cooperation.
national.staticLink: SAGAR means Security and Growth for All in the Region; the notes identify it as India’s maritime vision announced in 2015.
national.prelimsTakeaway: RAKSHA’s four pillars: Strategic Partnerships; Capacity Building; Indigenous Defence Exports; Maritime Security.
national.mainsAngle: Defence diplomacy can combine bilateral and multilateral cooperation with capacity building, maritime security and indigenous exports.
national.notes:
# 1. Document released
- **What:** **RAKSHA Defence Diplomacy Action Document** released by **Defence Minister Rajnath Singh** in **New Delhi** on **3 September 2026**.
- **Ministry:** **Ministry of Defence**
- **Status:** **Launched**

# 2. Roadmap and pillars
- **Duration:** **Ten-year** roadmap for **defence partnerships**, **security cooperation** and **defence manufacturing**.
| **Pillar** | **Focus** |
|---|---|
| **Strategic Partnerships** | **Defence partnerships** |
| **Capacity Building** | **Capacity building** |
| **Indigenous Defence Exports** | **Indigenous defence exports** |
| **Maritime Security** | **Indian Ocean cooperation**, **disaster assistance**, **anti-piracy efforts** and **Maritime Domain Awareness** |
- **Trap:** RAKSHA sets out a **roadmap**; do not treat its stated aims as completed projects or outcomes.

# 3. Background
- **SAGAR:** **Security and Growth for All in the Region**; India’s maritime vision announced in **2015** [GK].

> Exam angle: Identify the **Ministry** and recall RAKSHA’s **four pillars**, especially the elements of its maritime-security pillar.
